transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-29 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Michael Gomez (CISO, Trident), Anita Rao (Head of Infra, Trident), Evan Park (Platform Eng, Trident)

--- Summary ---
Jordan: quick round, we'll cover encryption at rest and in transit, KMS, BYOK and HSM options, and auditability.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everybody, thanks for taking the time. Quick introductions, and then we'll jump into the KMS and BYOK questions you sent over.
[00:12] Michael: Hey Jordan, thanks. I'm Michael Gomez, CISO at Trident Payments. We've got Anita and Evan with me. We're mainly focused on attestation for keys and who can see keys.
[00:22] Anita: Yep. Our compliance team is pushing for HSM-backed keys and strict key rotation policy, plus we need clear audit logs for any key access.
[00:30] Priya: Great, thanks. Quick note: Redwood supports multiple deployment modes - hosted, dedicated, and private - and we have a BYOK flow that can integrate with customer KMS or HSMs. We'll talk through the responsibilities and the audit surface.
[00:45] Evan: Real quick, are we talking customer-managed keys for data at-rest only, or do you also support TLS client certs / mutual TLS for in-transit encryption?
[00:53] Priya: We support TLS for in-transit, and for customer-managed keys we handle encryption at-rest for model artifacts, caches, and any persisted logs. If you need mutual TLS between your VPC and Redwood Private, that's also an option with the private deployment.
[01:10] Michael: Can you describe the BYOK flow end-to-end? Who holds the root key? Where do you generate DEKs?
[01:18] Jordan: Sure. Typical pattern: customer holds the CMK in their KMS/HSM. Redwood receives only wrapped data encryption keys (DEKs) that are encrypted under the CMK. DEKs are used inside the runtime but are stored encrypted. We support KMS callouts to AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, Google KMS, or customer HSM via PKCS#11 or equivalent.
[01:36] Anita: We're using an on-prem HSM appliance that speaks PKCS#11. We need the ability to rotate keys without downtime and need proof of HSM attestation. Does Redwood support attestation chains?
[01:48] Priya: We can support attestation metadata in the onboarding flow. For on-prem HSMs we commonly do an initial attest and capture the HSM certificate chain, and then use an integration user to perform wrap/unwrap ops. Rotation is orchestrated by you; Redwood can perform a rolling rewrap of DEKs with the new CMK with minimal impact, but you'd need to coordinate a maintenance window for the shortest path.
[02:10] Evan: Is the rolling rewrap automatic or manual? We can't afford a long outage.
[02:16] Priya: Rolling rewrap is automated on Redwood Private and Dedicated with a staged rewrap process that keeps old keys available until the new ones are stable; the runtime reads both until fully cutover. On hosted plans we coordinate with ops and have a similar sequence, but Dedicated/Private gives you more control.
[02:38] Michael: What about HSM key material exportability? Our policy forbids exporting private key material off the HSM.
[02:44] Priya: Understood. Our BYOK integration never exports private key material. We only accept wrapped DEKs; the CMK stays in your HSM. For PKCS#11 integrations we do calls that ask the HSM to perform wrap/unwrap and never request raw key bytes.
[02:59] Anita: Audit logs are critical. We need proof of every unwrap, including principal, timestamp, and calling host. Can Redwood provide key access audit logs or do we rely on our HSM logs?
[03:12] Jordan: Two places: Redwood emits application-level audit events (e.g., which service requested a decrypt) and you should continue to retain HSM-level logs for cryptographic ops. We can include the Redwood audit events in the trace and ship them to your SIEM via our audit-logs export.
[03:28] Evan: How granular are those logs? We need per-request context (request id, token user, route, model id).
[03:35] Priya: We include request id, service principal, route, model/version, and the operation (wrap/unwrap), though some low-level cryptographic metadata is only present in the HSM logs. We'll share a sample log schema.
[03:50] Michael: On the compliance side, we need to know about key rotation frequency — can Redwood force rotation, or do we keep control?
[03:59] Priya: You retain control of CMK rotation. Redwood can suggest rotation windows, and we support automated rewraps when you provide the new CMK or key version. For emergency revocation we also have a kill-switch to stop serving traffic to a model version, but the right pattern is rotate and rewrap.
[04:15] Jordan: Also want to flag token-level encryption for logs; we mask or encrypt PII in logs by default, and customers can opt to have logs zeroed in hosted plans; Dedicated/Private gives you full control and audit retention policy.
[04:30] Anita: We have to meet SOC 2 Type II with PCI considerations; is Redwood SOC 2? Do you have penetration test reports?
[04:37] Jordan: Yes, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II. We'll share the report; we also have periodic pen testing summaries available under an NDA or an attestation.
[04:49] Evan: Are there limitations around HSM-backed keys for model caching or the KV cache (K-V cache?)? We use heavy caching for low-latency inference.
[04:58] Priya: The runtime keeps encrypted K-V cache on disk and in-memory plaintext inside the process for active requests. DEKs for cache encryption are wrapped with your CMK. For very strict requirements, you can opt for an enclave-style deployment or Dedicated/Private where you manage the key unwrapping endpoints.
[05:20] Michael: About network segregation — can we restrict which Redwood hosts can request unwraps?
[05:26] Priya: Yes, when running Redwood Private in your VPC we can restrict endpoints and use VPC peering, security groups, and mutual TLS to lock down the unwrap flow. For Dedicated we offer private networking options and egress control.
[05:40] Anita: We use SAML SSO and fine-grained RBAC. How does Redwood map roles into key access?
[05:46] Jordan: Our RBAC ties into SSO (SAML/OIDC) and maps groups to roles. Key operations are gated by service principals and RBAC policies; humans don't directly call unwraps in normal operation. We'll provide a matrix mapping roles to capabilities (view, request decrypt, admin).
[06:05] Evan: A question on HSM vendor support — we saw HashiCorp Vault mentioned; do you integrate with Vault as an intermediary or only direct KMS/HSM?
[06:14] Priya: We support both patterns. You can use HashiCorp Vault as your wrapping provider and Redwood will call Vault's transit engine, or connect directly to the cloud KMS/HSM via standard APIs. For on-prem HSMs we support PKCS#11.
[06:28] Michael: Can you show proof of key attestation and the certificate chain? We'll need that for auditors.
[06:34] Priya: Yes, during onboarding we collect attestation metadata and a certificate chain snapshot. We can provide a signed attestation artifact for auditors. We'll redact sensitive fields if needed.
[06:46] Anita: Regs also require key usage separation — we want operators to not be able to see decrypted payloads. How do you achieve that?
[06:53] Priya: Principle of least privilege: decrypt operations happen inside ephemeral runtime sandboxes, and logs are sanitized. Access to raw decrypted payloads is restricted to a tiny set of service roles; human access is logged and requires approval. We can also integrate with KMS-based access controls so operators lack unwrapping privileges without explicit policy.
[07:15] Evan: On the topic of retention, how long do you keep audit logs and can we forward them to our SIEM?
[07:21] Jordan: We retain audit logs per your retention config. Default retention is 90 days for hosted; Dedicated/Private you can set retention and export to S3/ELK/Splunk. We provide connectors to forward logs or a push export API.
[07:36] Michael: For proof of concept, we'd like to run an HSM-backed BYOK pilot with a small traffic slice. What's the recommended approach?
[07:44] Priya: Start on Redwood Dedicated or Private with a small dedicated pool. We recommend instrumenting request-level tracing, enabling audit export to your SIEM, and running a staged rewrap test. Priya will run a bench to demonstrate latency delta when calling HSM for unwraps.
[08:00] Anita: Latency is a concern — HSM unwraps add milliseconds. What kind of latency impact should we expect?
[08:06] Priya: If every request calls the HSM on-path, you might see tens to low hundreds of ms added depending on your HSM and network. Our pattern is to cache unwrapped DEKs in memory for the runtime to avoid per-request HSM calls. With caching, unwraps happen on cache misses or rotation events, so steady-state latency impact is negligible. We'll share performance numbers from similar fintech customers.
[08:33] Evan: Do you support HSMs behind a proxy or gateway? Our HSM is in a restricted network.
[08:38] Priya: Yes, we support a gateway pattern. For Private deployments you can place the HSM in the same VPC and use internal network routes. For hosted we can set up a secure connector, but it requires network configuration and egress allowlisting.
[08:56] Michael: A compliance check: do you keep plaintext logs anywhere?
[09:00] Jordan: No plaintext PII is stored in logs by default; where needed we encrypt or redact. We can provide a data handling policy and examples.
[09:10] Anita: Does Redwood support KMS multi-region replication or key mirroring? We need cross-region availability without violating residency rules.
[09:19] Priya: We support multi-region key strategies. For strict residency, you can keep CMKs region-scoped and use regional Dedicated/Private endpoints. For availability we recommend a master CMK per region and rewrap strategy. We'll outline architecture options.
[09:36] Evan: Are there constraints for running model evaluation or dev workloads with BYOK?
[09:42] Priya: Dev workloads should use separate key material or a dev CMK; we recommend isolation. Evaluation environments can be configured to use test-only keys. We'll document recommended segregation.
[09:55] Jordan: Quick note — our compliance package includes a KMS integration checklist. I'll attach that in the follow-up along with the SOC 2 report.
[10:03] Michael: Cool. On the legal side, if we choose Dedicated or Private, do we need an amendment for BYOK/HSM responsibilities?
[10:11] Jordan: We'll have a security addendum that outlines responsibilities, access controls, and data handling obligations. Legal can review the SAA and we can mark sections specific to key custody.
[10:21] Anita: For the upcoming demo, can you show the audit logs for a sample unwrap operation?
[10:26] Priya: Yes, we can reproduce a sample with redacted values. I'll prepare a short runbook and a recorded demo that shows key events and the audit trail.
[10:37] Evan: Any known limits on number of keys or HSM connections?
[10:41] Priya: No hard key-count limits, but HSM connection quotas depend on vendor and your appliance. For scaling we recommend pooling strategies and rotating connection sessions. We'll share recommendations.
[10:56] Jordan: To recap — we'll share SOC2, KMS integration docs, sample logs, and schedule an HSM deep-dive. Priya will run a latency bench for unwraps. Customer to confirm availability for the week of Jan 11.
[11:12] Michael: That works. Thanks all.
[11:16] Jordan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the artifacts.

--- End of transcript ---

Referenced artifacts/links: SOC2 report (link to slack or secure share), KMS integration guide (attached in follow-up), HSM attestation process doc.
